issues.reason: 'The shift ends at dawn' is a verbal clause, so *Two kinds of clause* reifies an event, and the instruction set's own twin sentences settle it — 'the survey begins at dawn' / 'The harvest begins in September' are parsed as a reified begin event with the subject as Patient plus a Time atom and no tense — while Start/End stay pinned to from/to/until/since framing, as the 'When did X stop V-ing?' dual-storage note states outright (interval End from 'until <date>' versus a reified boundary event from the verb).

defect_summary: Compliant form: (Member sk_end_1 end) (Patient sk_end_1 sk_shift_1) (Member sk_shift_1 shift) (Time sk_end_1 dawn) — 'dawn' is a licensed day-part constant on Time — with no tense atom (bare present, unanchored adjunct, no TODAY) and no (End sk_shift_1 dawn) beside it, since one fact takes one head.
notes: The Intervals section names only the from/to/until/since wordings and never states the boundary against a boundary verb's own clause, so the flat-End reading is an understandable misread of a covered construction — an explicit line there would close it. Omitting the tense atom was correct under either reading.
